Next month's 26th marks the first anniversary of the Tai Po Wang Fuk Court fire. The independent committee investigating the fire is expected to submit its report to the Chief Executive before the end of October. Recent reports indicated that the government has activated the Head of Department Accountability System to investigate administrative responsibility for the fire and has redeployed Administrative Officers to assist. Chief Executive John Lee today (6th) did not respond to whether the mechanism has been activated, stating that the government has made a series of arrangements and will implement reforms and pursue accountability as soon as possible after the report is submitted. The Stanley luxury residence One Stanley has been exposed for having steel reinforcement that does not match the plans. Lee stated that the Buildings Department is investigating the case and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the investigation. With multiple construction projects being exposed for problems one after another, he said he attaches great importance to the construction quality of Hong Kong's building projects, as it concerns the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will strictly enforce the law.

Nearly a year after the Wang Fuk Court fire, the independent committee is expected to submit its report before the end of October. (File photo)

Earlier media reports stated that two Administrative Officers—former Deputy Secretary for Security Mok Kwan-yu and Commissioner for Sports Choi Kin-fan—would provide support work at an investigation小组 under the Public Service Commission, specifically responsible for preliminary work on administrative accountability.

Before attending the Executive Council meeting today, Chief Executive John Lee met the press. When asked whether the reports were true, and whether activating the Head of Department Accountability System to investigate responsibility means that even if there is a report, accountability involving officials will not yield immediate results, and how long the public must wait...

Lee stated that he made it clear from the start that after the independent committee submits its report, he will actively study and follow up on recommendations, implement reforms and announce details. He did not directly respond to whether Administrative Officers have already been redeployed to prepare preliminary investigation work, only saying that "the government has made a series of arrangements during this period," emphasising that after the report is submitted, based on its contents, "comprehensive reforms will be implemented as soon as possible in the short term, and accountability will be pursued," with detailed announcements to be made at that time.

Lee stated that after the independent committee submits its report, reforms and accountability will be pursued as soon as possible based on the report's contents. (File photo)

Lee also reiterated multiple times that improvement measures cannot wait. Therefore, when delivering the Policy Address in September, he announced seven priority improvement measures, including prohibiting smoking at construction sites, strengthening regulation of fire service installations, strengthening disciplinary actions and punishments for professionals and contractors, improving compliant operation of owners' corporations, studying the criminalisation of bid-rigging, providing tendering and evaluation services for the first time, establishing pre-qualification lists for consultants and contractors, and studying方案 to better assist the public with the professional aspects of construction projects.

According to records, the Public Service Commission is an independent statutory advisory body that advises the Chief Executive on civil service appointments, promotions and discipline matters. The Head of Department Accountability System was proposed by Chief Executive Lee in last year's Policy Address, establishing a two-tier investigation mechanism based on the severity of departmental issues. If the issue is less serious and involves an isolated incident, the first-tier investigation will be conducted by the Head of Department. If the department has serious problems, or involves widespread, recurring systemic issues, or may involve the role of the Head of Department, the second-tier investigation will be conducted by an investigation小组 led by the Public Service Commission.

The luxury residence One Stanley was exposed for having units with steel reinforcement that does not match the plans. Lee stated he would not comment on the case under investigation, and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the Buildings Department's investigation.

One Stanley steel reinforcement issue — Development Bureau requested to monitor investigation

Recently, construction projects have been exposed for problems one after another, including lift shaft tilting in the new block of Queen Mary Hospital, concrete samples in Tung Chung public housing not meeting strength standards, and floor slab steel reinforcement in Stanley luxury residence One Stanley not matching the plans. Lee was asked whether there are problems in construction and even project supervision...

He responded to the One Stanley project issue, stating that the Buildings Department is seriously investigating the case, "to ascertain whether construction quality and supervision were in place, and will handle it strictly in accordance with the law." As the investigation is still ongoing, he would not comment on the case details, and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the case investigation. However, he emphasised that he attaches great importance to the construction quality of Hong Kong's building projects, "paying attention to whether professionals related to the project have dutifully supervised, and whether contractors have violated regulations during construction," and stated that it concerns the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will inevitably strictly enforce the law.

He has also requested the Development Bureau to enhance legal regulatory requirements and penalties for overall construction projects, to ensure the deterrent effect of legislation, severely punish relevant personnel in violation, and safeguard the professionalism, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction projects. The Development Bureau will submit proposed amendments to the Buildings Ordinance this year to strengthen regulation and enhance the disciplinary system and penalties, and the authorities will pursue the relevant work at full speed.

The difficulty faced by nursing graduates in finding jobs has recently attracted attention. Lee stated that the demand for nurses has long existed, and pointed out that the Hospital Authority currently has more than 3,000 nurse vacancies, which graduates can apply for. (File photo)

Executive Councillor Cheung Yu-man criticises "unions impersonating people" — Lee states demand has long existed

The discussion on the difficulty of nurses finding jobs has heated up recently. The source was a radio phone-in programme after the Policy Address, in which a Mr. Kwok, who claimed to be a psychiatric nurse in a disciplinary force, said his application for deferred retirement was not approved, and that his daughter, a nursing graduate, became unemployed immediately after graduation, questioning the Hospital Authority's introduction of Mainland medical and nursing staff. Executive Councillor Cheung Yu-man subsequently questioned whether unions were "possibly impersonating people making phone calls," and stated he fully supports importing foreign talent.

When reporters asked how to solve the difficulty of nursing graduates finding jobs, and how to address the concentration of vacancies in senior nurses, and how to respond to Executive Councillor's remarks being accused of intensifying social conflicts, Lee stated that in every industry, there are situations where graduates do not immediately seek employment for various reasons after graduation, or where recruiting organisations select the most suitable candidates, "resulting in situations where certain individuals are not hired." He emphasised that society's demand for nurses has always existed, especially as Hong Kong's healthcare continues to develop and the population ages, "so recruitment numbers will ultimately inevitably reflect these existing demands." Without naming anyone, he also stated that "there are different discussions in society on this aspect, which allows everyone to discuss the issues more clearly."

Lee also stated that according to 2025/26 figures, there are approximately 4,000 potential nursing graduates, with about 2,500 actually applying to the Hospital Authority, meaning 1,500 applied for positions outside the Hospital Authority. The Hospital Authority currently still has more than 3,000 nurse vacancies, "nursing graduates can apply, and have the opportunity to be hired."

Secretary for Health Professor Lo Chung-mau earlier在接受訪問 with multiple media outlets, clarified that the government's recruitment policy definitely prioritises local talent. Lee also reiterated that based on the Hospital Authority's current nurse numbers, "99.8% are Hong Kong locally trained nurses," clearly implementing the policy of prioritising local talent in recruitment. He also stated that currently 40% of nurses work in the public healthcare system, with the remaining 60% in other healthcare positions, such as community nursing, elderly care, rehabilitation services, and private medical institutions. He emphasised that society's demand for nurses has long existed, and the government will, based on healthcare service needs, exchange views with the industry and academia, and do a good job in planning medical and nursing training and manpower development.
